Line 61 is the assertion the row went looking for. Running that file with --reporter=verbose prints, by name, «sc-animal-hazard — trace gate > SHADOW replays with ZERO violations (doc 76 §5)» passing. The same run prints the identical row for sc-lane-control-signal, the row's other named exception. Both «exceptions» are gated by the same loop, so the row is 0 for 2. WHY THE STATIC AUDIT MISSED IT — THE JOIN KEY, NOT THE GATE, IS WHAT IS ABSENT. grep -c "sc-animal-hazard" on that test file returns 0. The file never writes either id as a literal: it imports REELS from ../scReels and iterates `for (const reel of REELS)`, naming each describe block through a template literal (${reel.id} — trace gate), so the ids exist only at runtime. scReels.ts:475 is where sc-animal-hazard enters that array (districtId ov-solid-v1, names [shadow-correct, mistake-swerve-oncoming, mistake-cross-line]) and scReels.ts:487 is sc-lane-control-signal. The file is untouched by repair rounds 1–6 (fad8af6 … 769bfd4, all 2026-08) and predates the wave-c filing by four weeks. Nothing was fixed here; the row was wrong when it was written. The proof is source text plus a deterministic recorder. I used no verdict, no score, no star count and no live drive, so the eight-run non-determinism problem does not reach this row: a recorded trace on a fixed district replays to the same bytes every time, which the byte-identity assertion independently demonstrates.
